summary: Holds the canonical URL-scheme registry for storage paths. SCHEMES maps each canonical lowercase scheme (including '' for bare local paths) to a frozen SchemeSpec carrying aliases (gcs for gs, az for azure), a strict flag controlling mixed-case rejection, and the CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE it routes to. _ALIAS_TO_CANONICAL is derived from the aliases. Recognising a scheme does not imply a backend exists for it.
key_classes: SchemeSpec(scheme, aliases=(), strict=True, provider=None) — frozen metadata for a canonical URL scheme
extension_points: Add a SchemeSpec entry to SCHEMES (and aliases) to make a new URL scheme recognised by location.identify_scheme, StoragePath, detect_provider_from_path and the facade; a backend must be registered separately
lifecycle_notes: Stdlib + _core.constants only, so location.py and backend detection work on a base install
documentation_hooks: Supported schemes reference table (scheme, aliases, provider, backend status) for the path dispatch page
Maintainer checklist for adding a provider/scheme
examples: examples/path_dispatch/example.py — demonstrates scheme-to-provider detection that this table drives
risks: _ALIAS_TO_CANONICAL is underscore-private but imported across modules (location.py, path_helpers), so renaming it is a cross-module change
Schemes for Azure Files and NFS providers are absent: no URL routes to AZURE_FILES or NFS
README shows an 'r2://' scheme among S3-family examples; this table is the only source of the full list and is not rendered in user docs

evidence.detail: provider detection consults the scheme table via location.identify_scheme
